answer: Think of registration as a bridge toll that rises with traffic. A sybil farm spreads like a vine, pushing thousands of cheap shells across in one day, so the toll must surge with volume: the registration contract counts identities created in the last 24 hours on-ledger and sets the fee at $5 times one plus creations divided by 500, burned outright. On a quiet day with 200 creations the fee is $7, barely felt by honest newcomers. On a farm day with 10,000 creations it climbs to its summit of $105 each, $1,050,000 for the farm, and falls only when the daily count drops.
